# hybrid_demo: agent instructions

This is a Karni project. Karni already implements everything generic, so you write
only domain code.

An app with a game in it (kind `app+game` in pyproject.toml). The stack is set, so never
ask which technology to use: Python 3.12, Django 5.2, PostgreSQL, Redis and Celery, a
REST API on Django REST framework, and a React 18 + TypeScript app in `frontend/` on
@karni/ui whose pages host the game, its code in `frontend/src/game/` on the @karni/game
client. The server side is the karni-game module: players (guests first), saves, scores,
the wallet, daily content, achievements and remote config, mounted at `/api/game/`, with
its screens in the admin. The game is declared in `content/game.yaml` (`karni load`) and
its server hooks (save migrations, run checks) go in the `game.py` of an app. A project
`karni new --kind app+game` made has the game's page at `/game`, its hooks in
`games/game.py`, and `frontend/portal/`, which builds the game alone for the game
portals (`npm run game:package`). Never let the client decide coins, scores or unlocks:
the server does.

Before any work, run these two commands and follow what they return:

1. `karni context` prints the live inventory: apps, models, viewsets, UI components,
   hooks, pages, and every Karni module and built-in feature with whether the
   project has it (details: `karni modules show <name>`).
2. `karni rules` prints the conventions, each with a stable code (K###, or P### for
   the project's own).

While you work:

- Run `karni rules --check <file>` on every file you write and fix each violation it prints.
- Routine tasks are procedures: run `karni rules --procedure <name>` and follow every
  step. A request that starts with `/<name>` asks for that procedure, for the rest of
  the request:
  - `new-model`: Add a domain model the Karni way (model + viewset, nothing else)
  - `new-page`: Add a frontend page composing @karni/ui (50 lines or fewer)
  - `add-module`: Install an optional Karni module and wire it into settings
  - `new-module`: Create a new local Django app following Karni conventions
  - `site-from-design`: Build the public site from a designer's pages, with models and real content
  - `new-app`: Build an app from a one-line request: karni.yaml, then karni build
- To build an app from a one-line request (`/new-app <the request>`), follow the `new-app` procedure: karni.yaml first, then `karni build` (rule K311).
- Run `karni check` before committing. Every enforced rule fails the build.

If the `karni` command is unavailable, say so and stop. Do not guess the conventions.

## Module guidance

<!-- karni:module:game -->
## Games (karni-game)
- The server side of a game: `path("api/game/", include("karni_game.urls"))` before the
  API include, `KARNI_PEOPLE = True`. The client's contract is docs/game-api.md.
- Never write a player, save, score, wallet, ledger or achievement model of your own. A
  player is `Player.person` (karni.people). Find it from the request, never from an id.
- The server decides: never accept coins, XP, an unlock or a price from a client. A balance
  moves only through `karni_game.wallet.change` (atomic, capped, a ledger entry).
- Declare the game, its boards (`min_value`/`max_value` is the plausible range), currencies,
  rewards, items, achievements and missions in `content/game.yaml` (`karni load`).
- Save migrations and run checks go in `<app>/game.py` (`@hooks.save_migration`,
  `@hooks.run_check`). React to the game with its family events (`game.*`).
- A realtime server is your own service: it verifies the HS256 player token with
  `KARNI_GAME_SERVER_SECRET` and posts signed results to `<game>/multiplayer/results/`.
<!-- /karni:module:game -->
